name: Indusind Bank Ltd
title: Indusind Bank Ltd - 532187 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 PAT rose to Rs.1,037 crore from Rs.594 crore on lower credit costs, but normalised RoA is only 0.63% and the bank is still growing from a recalibrated base, with supply-side (capital, deposit) signals mixed.

summary.headline: IndusInd Q1 FY27 PAT rose to Rs.1,037 crore from Rs.594 crore QoQ, with GNPA at 3.25% and a 16.10% CET1 ratio.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as an inflection point, with deposits and advances growing 3.7% and 3.3% QoQ after a year of balance sheet recalibration. Profit after tax reached Rs.1,037 crore, helped by a one-off Rs.284 crore interest recovery on an income tax refund; excluding one-offs, RoA was 0.63%. Asset quality improved, with annualised net slippages at 1.50% and Rs.1,435 crore of write-offs, while microfinance stress moderated. Management reiterated an exit-FY27 RoA target of 1%, with about 60% of the improvement expected from PPOP and 40% from lower credit costs.

financial_highlights.change: includes Rs.284 crore one-off IT refund interest

segments.name: Vehicle Finance
segments.commentary: Book at Rs.99,718 crore, +3% YoY and flat QoQ; disbursements Rs.10,832 crore, down 4% YoY, with annualised net slippage at 2.01% vs 2.29% YoY. Management attributes Q1 weakness to seasonality, two-wheeler underwriting tightening and GST change.

segments.name: Micro Loans / Rural
segments.commentary: Micro loan book Rs.16,305 crore, -3% QoQ; gross slippages Rs.191 crore vs Rs.504 crore QoQ; 31-90 DPD at 0.6%. About 74% of the portfolio is covered under CGFMU guarantee. Merchant finance Rs.8,095 crore (+11% YoY), affordable housing Rs.2,889 crore (+21% YoY).

segments.name: Consumer Banking Assets
segments.commentary: Book at Rs.31,617 crore, +2% QoQ; consumer disbursements +16% QoQ. Home loans Rs.6,889 crore (+38% YoY, +6% QoQ); gold loans crossed Rs.1,200 crore; personal loans Rs.9,930 crore (-4% QoQ); credit cards Rs.9,418 crore (-3% QoQ). Annualised net slippage 4.19% vs 4.22% QoQ.

segments.name: SME Banking
segments.commentary: SME is about 13% of mix per analyst. LAP grew 8% QoQ and business loans 4% QoQ, net of migrations to wholesale. Management says foundations are being built and growth is intended to be significantly faster.

segments.name: Wholesale Banking
segments.commentary: Average wholesale loan book +7% QoQ, with management citing about 11% period-end growth and large corporates up 16% per the analyst's question. Corporate and SME fees +28% QoQ; transaction banking is 55% of wholesale and SME fees. A-and-above rated share steady at 82%; annualised gross slippage 0.17%.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: Average retail deposits (LCR basis) Rs.1,90,166 crore, +4% QoQ; retail share 49.5% vs 47.9% QoQ. NRI market share 3.6%. Affluent plus NRI deposits about Rs.85,000 crore, +2% QoQ.

guidance_outlook: Exit-FY27 RoA target of 1%; the bridge is about 60% from PPOP and 40% from lower credit costs, to be firmed up quarter by quarter.
Management expects grow in line with market in FY27 while maintaining an exit RoA of 1%.
NIM expected to see some pressure in Q2 and recover in Q3 and Q4 as high-yield businesses grow; NIM is a smaller contributor to the 1% RoA journey.
One-time ECL transition impact is still guided at 1% to 1.5% of loan book; the flow impact is seen as marginal; Basel changes effective 1 April 2027 offer capital offsets.
Microfinance is expected to accelerate meaningfully from Q2; other retail asset businesses should kick in over the next 3 quarters.
Board passed an enabling resolution for an equity capital raise of INR10,000 crore; management says no capital need at present.
capex_capacity: Digital and AI: over 12,000 employees trained; Indus Compass has 15,000+ monthly active users; ML models evaluate nearly half a million loan applications per month and monitor around 40 million customers hourly.
Vehicle finance: digital sourcing, Salesforce adoption and straight-through processing progressing; focus on underpenetrated geographies.
Consumer banking: leadership hires and investment in distribution, analytics and technology.
Deposit push: FCNR(B) mobilisation across retail FCNR(B), GIFT City and partner-bank lines.
demand_pricing: Wholesale: management cited ample opportunity across mid-corporate, large corporate and strategic corporate, with selection based on RAROC and reciprocity (transaction banking, current account floats, GST and salary accounts).
Deposit cost: cost of deposits 5.95%, about 150 bps above the closest peer per management; bulk term deposits cost about 50 bps more than retail, with outflow-rate weighting also considered.
Average CD ratio 83.0% vs 82.0% QoQ; average advances +2% QoQ and average deposits +1% QoQ.
Wholesale share of loan mix rose from 34% to 36%, which management says cut NIM by about 2 bps; RIDF addition cost about 1 bp.

qa_highlights.question: How different is the current wholesale growth profile from what was run down, and how should the retail/SME/corporate mix evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 82% of the wholesale portfolio is A-minus and above, and growth is a function of 6 to 9 months of capability building. Other engines (SME, vehicle, MFI) are also expected to grow, with growth optimised to meet ROA aspirations.

qa_highlights.question: How much further can cost of deposits fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is still a lot of work to do on deposit quantity and quality; the gap to the closest peer is about 150 bps, which it aims to narrow over the medium term. Mix shift toward retail and SBC deposits is also contributing, not just repricing.

qa_highlights.question: What portfolio actions are happening in retail and SME, and when will growth pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Microfinance disbursals were broadly flat QoQ despite seasonality, with acceleration expected from Q2. Retail asset disbursements rose 16% QoQ and should contribute over the next 3 quarters. Vehicle finance aims to regain lost market share over the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 8% QoQ fall in other expenses and what is the RoA bridge to 1%?
qa_highlights.answer: Statutory costs (DICGC, PSLC, CSR) and operating expenses fell; some disbursal-linked costs will rise later. The 0.63% to 1% bridge is seen as about 60% PPOP and 40% lower credit costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why not bid out more deposits given the asset yield, and how should the liability mix be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bulk deposits cost about 50 bps more, and institutional deposits carry 25-40% outflow rates versus 5-12% for retail. It will use bulk tactically and keep the core funding base driven by retail and SBC deposits to reduce ROA volatility.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL transition impact and will capital be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: The one-time transition impact is still guided at 1% to 1.5% of loan book, to be trued up by March. Capital offsets from Basel changes effective April 2027 are expected. At 16.1% CET1, management said capital raise is not urgent.

risks_watch: Stress in two-wheeler and tractor portfolios, which management has repeatedly flagged; fuel price rises and CV stress were questioned, though management says early trends show no building stress.
NIM pressure expected in Q2 as wholesale share rises; reported NIM was 3.35% normalised.
Deposit growth of only about 1% QoQ on an average basis against asset growth, with reliance on bulk deposits for wholesale growth.
ECL transition one-time impact of 1% to 1.5% of loan book, with EIR effects still to be firmed up.
Retail and SME growth still largely pending; consumer slippages and credit card and personal loan tail risk to be monitored.
Rs.10,000 crore enabling equity-raise resolution; timing and size not yet decided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the turnaround and balance sheet inflection, but guarded on timing for retail, SME and deposit-cost improvement. Management was candid that some growth is seasonal and that the NIM will be under pressure in Q2.
key_quotes: Q1 marked a clear inflection point for the Bank.
Our end of period deposits and advances grew 3.7% and 3.3% QoQ respectively reversing the moderation witnessed through much of the last financial year.

Excluding the one-off gains, RoA improved to 0.63% and we remain firmly focused on progressing towards our immediate target of RoA of 1%, supported by improving business momentum, lower credit costs and continued operating leverage.
Kunal, there is still a lot of work that we need to do on the deposit side, both on quantity and quality.
At 16.1% CET1, currently, that's not urgent in that sense.
So, if I do bid out it is about 50 basis points.

growth.why: Management reaffirmed an exit-FY27 RoA of 1% and said it will grow in line with the market in FY27, with about 60% of the RoA bridge from PPOP and 40% from lower credit costs; the brief gives no capacity additions or order numbers, and the FY27 revenue growth rate is not stated, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Normalised NIM 3.35% (-4 bps QoQ) with pressure guided in Q2, then recovery in Q3 and Q4 as high-yield businesses grow; cost of deposits 5.95% is about 150 bps above the closest peer, so repricing and mix shift give room, and the 0.63% to 1% RoA bridge is about 60% PPOP-led.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided to grow in line with the market in FY27; microfinance expected to accelerate from Q2 and retail asset businesses to kick in over the next 3 quarters, though average advances grew only 2% QoQ and deposits 1% QoQ.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Average CD ratio is 83.0%, and management said capital raise is not urgent at 16.1% CET1, with the Rs.10,000 crore equity enabling resolution having no stated need; no capex or utilisation-driven build-out was discussed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the exit-FY27 RoA target at 1% and gave no upgrade; normalised RoA is 0.63% against that 1% target, so there is a long bridge to close before any raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 NIM pressure is guided, the one-time ECL transition impact of 1% to 1.5% of loan book is still open, and two-wheeler and tractor stress has been flagged repeatedly, while the 1% exit RoA depends on credit costs falling (40% of the bridge).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Gold loans crossed Rs.1,200 crore, home loans grew 38% YoY and FCNR(B) and GIFT City deposit lines are being pushed, but no specific new product launch with a date was given.

rows.label: Deposit cost reduction toward peers
rows.why: Cost of deposits at 5.95% (-12 bps QoQ) is about 150 bps above the closest peer, and management aims to narrow the gap via retail and SBC mix, though it said there is still a lot of work to do.

rows.label: Exit-FY27 RoA of 1%
rows.why: Normalised RoA was 0.63% in Q1 (vs 0.45% QoQ) and management stands by a 1% exit target, with about 60% of the lift from PPOP and 40% from lower credit costs, to be firmed up quarter by quarter.

rows.label: Wholesale growth from mid and large corporate
rows.why: Average wholesale book grew 7% QoQ and management cites about 11% period-end growth, but capability building takes 6 to 9 months and the wholesale share rose from 34% to 36%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the RoA 1% exit target and balance sheet inflection, but cautious on retail, SME and deposit-cost timing and on Q2 NIM pressure; analysts pushed on the deposit-cost gap, the RoA bridge, and the ECL transition impact.
